query: What customer issues create the most support burden?

per_column.name: issue_category
per_column.rationale: Directly answers the query by giving a categorical axis to group and rank support burden by issue type. Sampled categorisations (billing, authentication, outage, feature_request, data) are all sound readings of the source text. A large 'other' bucket (52) slightly dilutes analytical leverage but the axis is genuinely useful.

per_column.name: burden_score
per_column.rationale: A composite burden metric is highly relevant to a 'support burden' query and enables ranking/modeling. However, the specific two-decimal values are opaque: their derivation is not transparent from the visible source, and priority/resolution_minutes could ground such a score, but the fine-grained precision (e.g. 29.24, 9.38) asserts a specificity not clearly warranted by the text alone. Values look plausibly correlated with severity (outage 32 > feature_request 4), so partially grounded but with unexplained precision.

judge.rationale: Both columns give genuine new axes for the 'support burden' query: issue_category enables grouping/ranking by problem type, and burden_score enables severity-weighted aggregation—neither is redundant with existing columns. issue_category is well grounded in the source text. burden_score is analytically apt and directionally consistent with severity, but its exact continuous values lack transparent derivation from the presented fields, introducing some ungrounded specificity. Overall strong on usefulness, moderate-to-good on groundedness.
